judged_text: Admin::EmbeddingController#update discards the request payload entirely and re-renders the current state, making PUT /admin/customize/embedding a persistence no-op that returns success. The admin-embedding controller's saveChanges action is wired to this endpoint, so any future settings UI or API client that PUTs embedding attributes receives a 200 while nothing is saved — an inert endpoint that should either accept attributes or not be routed.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds PUT /admin/customize/embedding routed to Admin::EmbeddingController#update (config/routes.rb) but that action ignores any request params and simply re-renders the current @embedding OpenStruct (app/controllers/admin/embedding_controller.rb), so the endpoint cannot persist changes. The Ember admin controller also includes a saveChanges action that calls this.get('embedding').update({}) (app/assets/javascripts/admin/controllers/admin-embedding.js.es6), reinforcing that a “save” endpoint exists even though it is a no-op. However, the current UI persists changes via Admin::EmbeddableHostsController (create/update/destroy) and the template doesn’t appear to call saveChanges, so this is more of an incomplete/misleading API surface than a presently broken feature.
